conditions.name: Night
conditions.definition: Images acquired at night or in darkness.

conditions.name: Low light
conditions.definition: Dim or insufficient lighting, low brightness, not necessarily at night.

conditions.name: Shadows
conditions.definition: Shadows cast on the code by structures, vehicles or people.

conditions.name: Uneven illumination
conditions.definition: Non-uniform lighting within one image: parts of the code are lit differently from others.

conditions.name: Illumination variation
conditions.definition: Lighting that changes between images (time of day, season, light source), named only generally.

conditions.name: Strong light / overexposure
conditions.definition: Excessive brightness, direct or strong sunlight, backlight or saturation.

conditions.name: Rain
conditions.definition: Rain during acquisition.

conditions.name: Snow
conditions.definition: Snowfall or snowy weather during acquisition (snow lying on the code is 'Snow cover').

conditions.name: Fog / haze
conditions.definition: Fog, haze or mist during acquisition.

conditions.name: Cloudy / sunny variation
conditions.definition: Changing sky conditions: sunny, partly cloudy, overcast.

conditions.name: Weather variation (unspecified)
conditions.definition: 'Various', 'extreme' or 'rough' weather named without saying which.

conditions.name: Rust / corrosion
conditions.definition: Rust or corrosion on or around the code.

conditions.name: Dirt / stains
conditions.definition: Dirt, dust, mud, smear, oil, soiling or other contamination on the code.

conditions.name: Faded / peeling paint
conditions.definition: Faded, discoloured, peeled or worn-off paint of the characters.

conditions.name: Damaged / deformed characters
conditions.definition: Scratched, dented, broken, deformed, deteriorated or partially erased characters, or a damaged container surface.

conditions.name: Missing characters
conditions.definition: Characters physically missing from the code (worn away or never printed).

conditions.name: Vertical codes
conditions.definition: Codes written vertically, character under character.

conditions.name: Rotated / tilted / skewed codes
conditions.definition: In-plane rotation, tilt, skew, slant or inclination of the code or its characters.

conditions.name: Viewing angle / perspective
conditions.definition: Oblique camera viewpoint, changing perspective, side views, perspective distortion.

conditions.name: Lens distortion
conditions.definition: Optical distortion by the lens (fish-eye, wide angle).

conditions.name: Other text / markings near the code
conditions.definition: Other characters, texts, logos, labels, warning signs, weight data or licence plates competing with the code.

conditions.name: Structural parts near the code
conditions.definition: Door bars, hinges, locks, rods, levers, pipes, grips or frames crossing or adjoining the code.

conditions.name: Corrugated surface
conditions.definition: Corrugated, wavy or curved container walls whose texture competes with the text and bends the characters.

conditions.name: Complex background / scene
conditions.definition: Cluttered, complex or busy backgrounds and port scenes around the ILU.

conditions.name: Multiple codes per image
conditions.definition: Several ILUs or several codes in one image.

conditions.name: Check-digit frame
conditions.definition: The box printed around the check digit, which merges with or disturbs the digit.

conditions.name: Multi-line codes
conditions.definition: The code is split over two or more lines.

conditions.name: Variable code arrangement / format
conditions.definition: Several arrangement formats of the characters: rows, columns, groupings, alignment modes.

conditions.name: Variable code position
conditions.definition: The placement of the code on the ILU differs between units.

conditions.name: Variable character spacing
conditions.definition: Irregular gaps between characters or groups, including blanks inside the code.

conditions.name: Small characters / low resolution
conditions.definition: Characters too small in the image, or imaged at too low a resolution.

conditions.name: Long camera distance
conditions.definition: A long camera-to-ILU distance.

conditions.name: Character size variation
conditions.definition: Codes or characters of widely varying size or scale across images.

conditions.name: Motion blur
conditions.definition: Blur caused by the motion of the vehicle, the ILU or the camera.

conditions.name: Blur (cause unspecified)
conditions.definition: Blurred or unclear images with no cause given, or defocus.

conditions.name: Camera shake
conditions.definition: Shaking or vibration of the camera.

conditions.name: Occlusion by objects
conditions.definition: Part of the code hidden by objects, seals, cables, trucks, other ILUs, people or equipment.

conditions.name: Snow cover
conditions.definition: Snow lying on the code.

conditions.name: Truncated / partially visible code
conditions.definition: Part of the code outside the image or the field of view, or not complete in a single frame.

conditions.name: Image noise
conditions.definition: Sensor, transmission or stripe noise in the image.

conditions.name: Low image quality (unspecified)
conditions.definition: Poor, degraded, compressed or indistinct images without a named cause.

conditions.name: Glare / reflection
conditions.definition: Specular reflections or glare on the container surface or from light sources.

conditions.name: Text polarity (light or dark characters)
conditions.definition: Characters may be light on dark or dark on light.

conditions.name: Low code-to-surface contrast
conditions.definition: Little contrast between the character colour and the surface colour.

conditions.name: Colour variation (text / container)
conditions.definition: Varying colours of the characters, the container or the background.

conditions.name: Font variation
conditions.definition: Different fonts, typefaces, stencils or handwriting.

conditions.name: Similar-looking characters
conditions.definition: Confusable characters such as 0/O, 1/I, 8/B, 2/Z, 6/G.

conditions.name: Touching or overlapping characters
conditions.definition: Characters printed so close that they touch or overlap, or adjacent text lines that merge.

conditions.name: Character segmentation errors
conditions.definition: Broken strokes, split or merged segments, information lost in binarisation or thinning.

conditions.name: Detection / localisation errors
conditions.definition: Missed, imprecise or spurious detections of the code region, and errors propagated between stages.

conditions.name: Code split by word-level detection
conditions.definition: A space-separated code fragmented into word-level boxes by a generic text detector.

conditions.name: Code format / sequence issues
conditions.definition: Errors tied to the code format: check-digit ambiguity, letter/digit confusion against the format, out-of-vocabulary or long sequences, mixed letters and digits.

conditions.name: Acquisition failures
conditions.definition: Missing views, mistimed triggers or other capture failures.

conditions.name: Scope limitations
conditions.definition: Cases the method excludes by design, e.g. codes on the roof or tank containers.

iluTypes.name: Containers
iluTypes.definition: ISO 6346 freight containers of any size or kind (dry, standard, high-cube); container codes, container numbers, BIC or ISO codes all denote this type.

iluTypes.name: Semi-trailers
iluTypes.definition: Road semi-trailers or trailers that carry an ILU identification code (EN 13044); a truck or chassis that merely carries a container is not this type.

iluTypes.name: Railway wagons
iluTypes.definition: Rail wagons, railcars or freight cars whose own wagon number is identified (not an ILU).

studies.Title: Advanced Text Detection of Container Numbers via Dual-Branch Adaptive Multi-Scale Network
studies.Venue: Applied Sciences
studies.Contributions:
- Combines Efficient Multi-Scale Attention with Differentiable Binarisation (DBNet)
- Auxiliary information branch that uses OTSU thresholding to remove noise
- Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) in the feature pyramid
- Dual-loss strategy (BCE loss and Dice loss, weighted)
studies.Contributions evidence: The DAMNet integrates Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) into the Differentiable Binarization (DBNet) model to address the challenges of improving accuracy and efficiency in the current text detection networks. | We also incorporate an auxiliary information branch that processes images using the Otsu thresholding method to extract local features. | Furthermore, we improve the feature pyramid structure by introducing Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF). | We also propose a dual-loss strategy. | It employs BCE loss for classification tasks and Dice loss to tackle imbalanced positive and negative samples.
studies.Main approach evidence: This paper proposes DAMNet, enhancing the DBNet text detection model.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: To address the problem of container number detection in natural scenes, we propose DAMNet.
studies.Method architecture evidence: The network consists of the following three main components: a dual-branch feature extraction network based on ResNet18, a multi-scale adaptive feature fusion module, and a binarization post-processing module.
studies.Methods:
- DBNet-based text detector with a dual-branch ResNet18 backbone
- Main branch with Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA)
- Auxiliary branch fed with Otsu-binarised images
- Feature fusion: FPN with Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF)
- Loss: weighted BCE and Dice loss
studies.Methods evidence: Both the main and the auxiliary information branches utilize Residual Network 18 (ResNet18) [2]. | Additionally, EMA is integrated into the residual network within the main branch. | Then, the binarized image is used as the input for the auxiliary information branch. | This paper combines the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) [29] with ASFF in the feature fusion phase. | This strategy combines the binary cross entropy loss(BCE loss) [30] for addressing classification issues with the Dice loss, with both being integrated through weighting.
studies.Method class evidence: This paper proposes DAMNet, enhancing the DBNet text detection model. | In the auxiliary information branch, to effectively reduce the interference of background noise in the container number text detection task, we adopt the Otsu [31] thresholding method to binarize the original container number text image. | Then, the binarized image is used as the input for the auxiliary information branch.
studies.Dataset origin evidence: Given the current lack of publicly available datasets for container number text in academia, we have constructed a custom dataset specifically for container number recognition to comprehensively evaluate the generalization ability and robustness of the research presented in this paper. | Extensive testing is conducted on the International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition 2015 (ICDAR2015) dataset [6] and a self-collected dataset of container numbers to validate the network's effectiveness.
studies.Dataset availability evidence: Data Availability Statement: The data are available upon request from the corresponding author.
studies.Number of images evidence: It includes over 3000 text images captured at different angles on wooden crates of varying shapes.
studies.Containers evidence: Given the current lack of publicly available datasets for container number text in academia, we have constructed a custom dataset specifically for container number recognition to comprehensively evaluate the generalization ability and robustness of the research presented in this paper. | To validate the advancements of our algorithm, we conduct comparative experiments between our presented method and state-of-the-art general natural scene text detection methods on the ICDAR2015 dataset, CTW1500, and our custom container number dataset, utilizing a standardized evaluation metric.

studies.Title: Confidence-Guided Shipping Container Code Recognition Using Deep Learning
studies.Venue: Big Data and Cognitive Computing
studies.Contributions:
- dataset development
- localisation network (CCLN) that replaces the sliding-window output with bounding-box regression and needs no post-processing
- container code recognition
studies.Contributions evidence: [Highlights] Development of a singular dataset for Localization and Recognition of container code. | We developed the first-stage Container Code Localization Network (CCLN), which modifies the output from sliding windows to bounding box regression, as demonstrated in [33]. | This model eliminates post-processing steps such as ASA and AMSR, and loss function previously used in [52]. | We developed the second-stage Container Code Recognition Network (CCRN) to optimize performance without compromising feature integrity, thereby avoiding feature loss or increased computational complexity, as discussed in [13].
studies.Main approach evidence: The CCLN processes rear-view images of containers to predict the container code region, which is defined by a bounding box that includes (1) the owner code and category identifier, (2) the serial number, and (3) the check digit. | The CCRN processes the cropped image and converts the visual container code into a machine-readable format, facilitating accurate and efficient recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: In our paper, we introduce an ACCLR system that consists of two main models: the localization model, CCLN, and the recognition model, CCRN. | The two models were trained separately for the newly designed system and one in [6, 21], with the localization model trained using container code dataset bounding labels and the recognition model trained using cropped container codes and scene text labels.
studies.Method architecture evidence: The CCLN model is based on the architecture proposed in [52], utilizing ResNet [14] and UNet [37] to deliver high detection accuracy while maintaining a compact and efficient design. | The CCRN model, on the other hand, incorporates CNN [28], RNN [7], and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) [11], following the architecture outlined in [39].
studies.Methods:
- Text detection: CCLN (ResNet50 with UNet skip connections, bounding-box regression, IoU loss)
- Text recognition: CCRN (CRNN: CNN, BiLSTM, CTC)
studies.Methods evidence: The Localization Model Architecture incorporates the ResNet50 block, with skip connections inspired by UNet [37] that help preserve information throughout the architecture. | The CCLN was trained using the Intersection over Union (IoU) loss function, which evaluates the overlap between the predicted and ground truth bounding boxes. | In sequence recognition, the bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) [16] layer outputs the probability distribution of all characters in our character set per time frame. | It is also important to note that this entire recognition model is called CRNN, which was first introduced in [39].
studies.Method class evidence: The CCLN model is based on the architecture proposed in [52], utilizing ResNet [14] and UNet [37] to deliver high detection accuracy while maintaining a compact and efficient design. | The CCRN model, on the other hand, incorporates CNN [28], RNN [7], and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) [11], following the architecture outlined in [39].
studies.Camera position evidence: The rear-view images of shipping containers were captured by a camera positioned on the top right side of each container. | These include tilted, low-quality, noisy, and deformed container code images with varying font sizes as containers move towards or away from the camera.
studies.Dataset origin evidence: This dataset was created by combining a subset of images from datasets released by [30] and [29], augmented with images captured under various environmental and lighting conditions. | Fifty percent of the images in our experimental dataset were sourced from these two datasets.

studies.Contributions evidence: To address this gap, we present the TRUDI dataset—a comprehensive collection comprising 35,034 annotated instances across five categories: container, tank container, trailer, ID text, and logo. | The images were captured at operational ports using both ground-based and aerial cameras, under a wide variety of lighting and weather conditions. | For the identification of TUs—which involves reading the 11-digit alphanumeric ID typically painted on each unit—we introduce TITUS, a dedicated pipeline that operates in three stages: (1) segmenting the TU instances, (2) detecting the location of the ID text, and (3) recognising and validating the extracted ID. | The output is then verified for ISO6436 compliance and associated with the TU. | We conducted experiments using TRUDI and its subsets (aerial, ground, and combined perspectives) to evaluate the three stages of TITUS and establish a baseline.

studies.Venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
studies.Contributions:
- Practical Unified Network (PUN): one encoder-decoder network with rough detection of the second code part, semantic segmentation of the three code parts and the type code, and single-character classification
- RoIResize module without learnable parameters (crop and resize of feature maps) that bridges the modules for end-to-end training
- Lightweight model (15.53 million parameters, 4.86 FPS at 768 × 768) deployed at smart gates of Shanghai Port
- Annotated dataset of 5877 gate images with horizontal and vertical codes
studies.Contributions evidence: We design an end-to-end network, whose core structure is an encoder-decoder for input feature learning. | In addition, an efficient RoIResize module that does not require learning is introduced and used to bridge the three modules to realize the error backward propagation and construct an end-to-end PUN model. | Parameter size of our model is only 15.53M, which takes up little GPU memory and is suitable for deployment in industrial scenarios. | Our model has been deployed and running in multi smart gates of Shanghai Port for nearly a year, showed certain practical application capabilities. | The dataset contains 5877 images of the gate working scene with a size of 1080×1920 including horizontal and vertical container code and type.
studies.Main approach evidence: The model is based on the encoder-decoder network, which integrates the detection of the second part of container code, the semantic segmentation of the three parts of container code and type, and the classification of single character features of container code and type. | We propose an encoder-decoder network structure, which integrates detection, semantic segmentation and classification modules to achieve end-to-end container code and type recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: It returns fixed size feature maps by performing crop and resize operations on feature maps of a specific area, which facilitates the end-to-end training of the network. | The loss for the whole PUN model for training is as follows:
studies.Method architecture evidence: Encoder first encodes an RGB image of size H × W to obtain the 4-stage CNN features. | Considering that more model parameters need more GPU memory consumption, we chose ResNet18 as the backbone of the encoder, Unet++ as the segmentation method, and only one fully-connected layer for classification module, so our PUN has only 15.53M parameters, which is about twice less than DeepSolo, the end-to-end recognition model with the second smallest number of parameters.
studies.Methods:
- ResNet18 encoder with a rough detection head for the second part of the code (horizontal/vertical)
- RoIResize to crop and resize the expanded region on the feature maps
- Unet++ decoder for segmenting the three code parts and the type code
- Isolation of the characters from the segmented areas (equal division)
- Single-character classification (fully connected layer, 36 classes)
studies.Methods evidence: Rough detection module consists of an Encoder and a rough detection head as shown in Fig. 5. | It returns fixed size feature maps by performing crop and resize operations on feature maps of a specific area, which facilitates the end-to-end training of the network. | The encoder of our semantic segmentation module is shared with the backbone of rough detection module, and the decoder is implemented with reference to Unet++ [26]. | Next, we equally divide the 4 blocks into 4, 6, 1, and 4 pieces according to actual length of the parts to obtain single character locations, and with these locations, we could get the corresponding single character feature maps. | After the operations of isolation module, all single character features can be obtained, so single character classification can be performed through the Classification Head.
studies.Method class evidence: The Encoder-Decoder, Rough detection head, Segmentation head and Classification head in the PUN model are trainable, and the RoIResize and Isolation module do not need to be learned. | For inference, the minimum bounding boxes of each pixel blocks with value of 5, 6, 7, 8 can be obtained respectively through the cv2.minAreaRect algorithm in Opencv. | Next, we equally divide the 4 blocks into 4, 6, 1, and 4 pieces according to actual length of the parts to obtain single character locations, and with these locations, we could get the corresponding single character feature maps.

studies.Contributions evidence: The proposed model uses two important models: (1) the localization model, based on Resnet [6] and U-net [18], and (2) the recognition model, based on CRNN [19] to provide an inventive method for automated shipping container code localization and recognition. | By lowering the number of layers in the model proposed in [24] localization model and eliminating the feedback loop and noise reduction method, the main contribution is to simplify the network design. | These modifications lead to a notable decrease in processing costs, yet the proposed system performs similarly to the one presented in [24]. | Furthermore, the proposed localization model exhibits enhanced versatility by detecting both horizontal and vertical container codes.
studies.Main approach evidence: The container code localization model, leveraging ResNet and U-Net, processes a rear-view container image to identify three bounding boxes for code components (owner code & category identifier, serial number, and check digit). | The cropped text image is then sent into the recognition model, which transforms it into a format that can be read by machines.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The proposed model uses two important models: (1) the localization model, based on Resnet [6] and U-net [18], and (2) the recognition model, based on CRNN [19] to provide an inventive method for automated shipping container code localization and recognition. | The identified regions are then cropped, converted to grayscale, and resized with white padding to meet the input requirements of the recognition model.
studies.Method architecture evidence: Feature extraction employs Resnet, and the subsequent upscaling counters the reduction in feature map size. | The container code recognition model integrates CNN and RNN into a CRNN architecture, as depicted in Figures 4 and 5. | The results are then passed through a Connectionist Temporal Classifier (CTC) decoder to remove duplicates.

studies.Contributions evidence: This paper proposes a practical end-to-end, real-time deployable ACCR system that runs at an inference speed of 31.72 frames per second (fps) with an end-to-end accuracy of 89.20%. | Several other neural networks such as Single-Shot Arbitrarily Shaped Text Detector (SAST) and Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) with Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) feature have been studied and investigated to identify their inherent strength and weakness in addressing STR problems. | The post-processing algorithm is developed and added at the end of the pipeline to validate the recognized CCCs with the detected check digit according to the ISO 6346 standard. | The ACCR system has been dockerized to reduce dependencies during installation. | Code is available at: https://github.com/laulj/CCCR.
studies.Main approach evidence: An automatic container code identification involves two main processes which are text detection and text recognition. | The end-to-end pipeline combines DB as its localization module and SRN as its recognition module.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The proposed ACCR system in this work is comprised of two main modules, localization and recognition. | After localizing the CCC instances by DB, SRN is then employed to extract the code characters for recognition.
studies.Method architecture evidence: The localization module involves implementing a DB module (without the adaptive scale fusion feature) [6] into the training of a ResNet-50 backbone to improve the CCC localization accuracy, while an end-to-end trainable SRN [7] is chosen for the recognition task because of its ability to capture and integrate the semantic context of the text instances to improve the predictions on STR. | SRN is a semantic context modeled end-to-end neural network introduced by Yu, Deli, et al. that integrates a transformer to enhance the visual encoding features and capture the semantic context of the text instances [7]. | As demonstrated in Fig. 4, SRN composes of four modules: an FPN aggregated ResNet-50 backbone network, parallel visual attention module (PVAM), global semantic reasoning module (GSRM), and visual-semantic fusion decoder (VFSD).
studies.Methods:
- Text detection: Differentiable Binarisation (DB) with ResNet-50 backbone, fine-tuned (compared with SAST)

- Post-processing: ISO 6346 check-digit validation
studies.Methods evidence: The localization module involves implementing a DB module (without the adaptive scale fusion feature) [6] into the training of a ResNet-50 backbone to improve the CCC localization accuracy, while an end-to-end trainable SRN [7] is chosen for the recognition task because of its ability to capture and integrate the semantic context of the text instances to improve the predictions on STR. | The end-to-end pipeline combines DB as its localization module and SRN as its recognition module. | Due to the sequential left-to-right reading nature of recognition models, all cropped images with a height-to-width ratio exceeding 1.5 are rotated 90 degrees anticlockwise prior to being fed into the recognition model. | The post-processing algorithm is developed and added at the end of the pipeline to validate the recognized CCCs with the detected check digit according to the ISO 6346 standard.

studies.Venue: Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
studies.Contributions:
- Structured scene-text spotting task conditioned on a regular expression
- STEP: regex-guided transformer text spotter extending TESTR

studies.Contributions evidence: We introduce the structured scene-text spotting task, which requires a scene-text OCR system to spot text in the wild according to a query regular expression. | The Structured TExt sPotter (STEP), a network where the detection and the recognition processes are guided with a queried regular expression. | Our dataset includes 836 images where 6 types of formatted text have been annotated. | We perform comprehensive experimentation and ablation studies, and demonstrate that our approach outperforms state of the art scene-text baselines.
studies.Main approach evidence: The STEP architecture is based on TESTR [32], an end-to-end framework for generic text detection and recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: We propose instead to train a single model that can dynamically condition both the detection and recognition stages on a user provided regular expression (regex). | The STEP architecture is based on TESTR [32], an end-to-end framework for generic text detection and recognition.
studies.Method architecture evidence: This architecture is composed of an encoder and two decoder networks based on the transformer [29]. | The features extracted by a CNN are the input to a Deformable DETR-like [34] encoder.
studies.Methods:
- STEP: end-to-end text spotter based on TESTR (CNN backbone, Deformable DETR encoder, character decoder and location decoder)
- Query regular expression encoded as multi-hot vectors and injected through cross-attention layers in the encoder and both decoders
- Detection confidence computed from character and location sub-queries
- Trained on a HierText-derived dataset with merged annotations that contain spaces (TESTR pre-trained weights); zero-shot on the test set
- Baselines: TESTR, SwinTextSpotter and ABCNet v2 with merging and filtering post-processing
studies.Methods evidence: The STEP architecture is based on TESTR [32], an end-to-end framework for generic text detection and recognition. | This structure is queried as a regular expression, which we represent using a series of multi-hot encoded vectors. | To address this, STEP utilizes both location and character sub-queries to produce the confidence score. | Our training and evaluation strategy uses a modified version of HierText to create our training and validation splits. | We compare our approach with TESTR [32], SwinTextSpotter [8] and ABCNet v2 [20], three generic state-of-art scene-text models we use as baselines.

studies.Venue: Journal of Real-Time Image Processing
studies.Contributions:

- Multiple Reuse Feature Pyramid Networks (MRFPN) neck for better feature fusion

studies.Contributions evidence: First, for container code localization, the backbone component consists of MobileOne blocks to enhance feature extraction capability and accelerate inference speed. | Second, for container code recognition, a lightweight MobileNetV3 is used as the backbone. | Third, a feature extraction module, called Multiple Reuse Feature Pyramid Networks (MRFPN), is designed to extract sufficient semantic information. | The proposed method significantly reduces parameters, computational costs, and model size while maintaining high accuracy, and greatly improves inference speed.
studies.Main approach: Text detection, character detection and character recognition
studies.Main approach evidence: This paper adopts a deep learning-based object detection algorithm, dividing container code recognition into two stages: container code localization and container code recognition, with the latter being transformed into a classification problem of letters and numbers. | In this stage of the proposed algorithm, the input images used are the cropped images after the first step of container code localization detection, with a size of 224*X pixels depending on the detection position.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The proposed method consists of two stages: container code localization and container code recognition.
studies.Method architecture evidence: For container code localization and recognition, the network framework based on YOLOV5 is used and adapted to mobile devices.
studies.Methods:
- Code localisation: YOLOv5 with MobileOne backbone (multi-branch in training, merged to a single branch at inference), CBAM attention and MRFPN neck; three region classes
- Character recognition: YOLOv5 with MobileNetV3 backbone and depthwise separable convolutions on the cropped regions
- Mosaic data augmentation for increasing training data diversity
studies.Methods evidence: In the container code localization stage, the algorithm is enhanced by integrating the MobileOne module based on the RepVGG method and the CBAM mechanism into the backbone section, which effectively enhances the representation capability of the feature map by adjusting the channel and spatial weights of the feature map to identify the most relevant features in the image. | During inference, the multiple branch structures are converted into a single-branch structure to accelerate inference speed. | In the container code recognition stage, the lightweight MobileNetV3 module is adopted in the backbone section, which has fewer parameters and a smaller model size, while maintaining high accuracy. | Moreover, depthwise separable convolution replaces regular convolution throughout the algorithm, which further reduces the network's size and computational cost, making it more suitable for real-time applications. | The Mosaic technique is utilized during the training process to increase the diversity of the training data, which generates more variations and enables the model to better adapt to different scenes and lighting conditions. | [Fig. 13: the three region classes of the localisation stage] Fig. 13 Simulate the detection effect of complex situations. a Original, b Flip Horizontal, c Excessive brightness, d Brightness too low, e Motion blur, f Rain, g Fog, h Snow (1—Container Code and Check Digit, 2—Container Size and Type Code, and 3—Container Owner Code)

studies.Contributions: End-to-end system (text detection + character detection + classification, post-processing like check digit, type-size code checking)
studies.Contributions evidence: In this study, we provide a complete solution to container code recognition including character region location, character detection and classification, type code recognition, checking digit number with rules and ensemble methods. | Moreover, we check the digit number according to the ISO rules and improve the recognition accuracy via incorporating the ensemble method.
studies.Methods:

- Character detection: multi-scale sliding window with Random Ferns on HOG features, non-maximal suppression
- Character classification: two SVMs (letters, digits) with RBF kernel on Sobel edge-density features
- Type code: Pictorial Structures over the detected characters
- Ensemble over the code areas of a container (plurality vote, sum rule) and check-digit verification
studies.Methods evidence: We use the high-pass filter to detect the vertical edges. | Meanwhile, we perform multi-scale character detection via sliding window classification (Random Ferns [2]). | We use the Sobel operator to generate the features and feed them into two SVM classifiers (one is for letter and another is for digit). | For the type code recognition, we treat them as “word” and design the Pictorial Structures [10] formulation that optimizes the configuration via taking the locations and scores of detected characters as input. | We develop two combination rules for making the decisions in ensemble: character-level combination by plurality vote and confidence-level combination by the sum rule.

studies.Contributions:
- Adaptive deep learning framework for shipping container code localisation (ResNet and U-net) and recognition (CRNN)
- Adaptive score aggregation (ASA) algorithm that removes low-confidence and noisy text proposals

studies.Contributions evidence: In this article, we propose an adaptive deep learning framework for shipping container code localization and recognition. | In the adaptive deep learning framework, we propose an adaptive score aggregation (ASA) algorithm to clean the low confident and noisy localization proposals. | Different from the traditional ACCR framework, the localization outputs in our adaptive framework can be adjusted in a range given by our designed average to maximum suppression range (AMSR) algorithm. | A better code localization performance can be achieved by constructing localization deep neural networks and properly defining the loss in the training process.
studies.Main approach evidence: We construct our localization model based on Resnet [26] and U-net [27] and recognition model based on CRNN [19]. | CRNN [19] is used to recognize a sequence of text without splitting the input images into single character images.

studies.Method architecture evidence: We adopt Resnet [26] as the backbone in the feature extraction process. | CRNN model consists of three parts, sequence feature extraction by CNNs, sequence scoring by recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and sequence translation by connectionist temporal classification (CTC) [29].
studies.Methods:

- Check against ISO 6346: if the combined code does not meet the standard, the next boundary set (maximum, minimum, mean) is tried

studies.Contributions:
- Developed a full system for container code detection and recognition with robust handling of code variations.
- Proposed a ResNet50-based FCN detector for localising container codes.
- Introduced a CRNN-based recogniser to directly read code sequences (without character segmentation).
- Introduced a dedicated check digit detector for improved accuracy.

studies.Contributions evidence: To improve the efficiency of container number identification, this paper proposes a high-robust automatic container code localization and recognition system via an efficient code detector and sequence recognition in response to the variance of container types and shooting conditions with about 0.1s per-frame and 93.98% overall accuracy. | A full convolutional neural network along with a container code segmentation to localize the code in 720p images. | A convolutional recurrent neural network to simplify the combination of the code patch extraction and identification process. | We build a 3-layer convolutional neural network to detect the check digit separately. | After multiprocessing optimization, a system implemented with the proposed method can reach 12 FPS on a 720p video stream.
studies.Main approach evidence: This detector localizes the text in the overall picture, and then feed the result into a code segmentation to extract the three parts of the container code. | This paper follows the pipeline of CRNN[14] to propose a method to recognize the container code in patches with variant lengths, eliminating the time for character segmentation.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The detector in Section III outputs the localization of the container code and divides it into three parts. | Since the non-maximum suppression part of the box number location algorithm cannot apply backpropagation, this paper trains two parts of the detector separately.

studies.Contributions:

studies.Contributions evidence: This paper proposes a novel Container Text Detection and Recognition Network (CTDRNet) for accurately detecting and recognizing container scene text. | The CTDRNet consists of three components: (1) CTDRNet text detection enables to improve detection accuracy for single words; (2) CTDRNet text recognition has faster convergence speed and detection accuracy; (3) CTDRNet post-processing improves detection and recognition accuracy. | The CTDRNet improves the convergence speed and detection accuracy with our designed Container Text Detection Basic Network (CTDBNet) and Container Text Recognition Basic Net (CTRBNet). | The CTDRNet post-processing discards text boxes with the probability less than 0.6, which effectively reduces the rate of false detections and increases two percentage points on our test set.
studies.Main approach evidence: Container text recognition could be divided into two phases: text detection and recognition. | Phase 1 - CTDRNet text detection precisely localizes a single text. | Phase 2 - CTDRNet text recognition recognizes the detected words and converts image sequences into variable-length sequences.

studies.Contributions:
- Detection and recognition modules that each combine two branches: MSER and CTPN for detection, character segmentation with ResNet and CRNN for recognition
- Check-digit verification to choose between the two recognition results
- Online training: combined detection results and verified or corrected codes update CTPN and CRNN at runtime
studies.Contributions evidence: The detection module applies both algorithms based on computer vision and neural networks, and generates a better detection result through combination to avoid the drawbacks of the two methods. | The recognition module exploits both character segmentation and end-to-end recognition, and outputs the recognition result which passes the verification. | By combining several algorithms, the system is able to deal with more situations, and the online training mechanism can improve the performance of the neural networks at runtime.
studies.Main approach evidence: The proposed container-code recognition system consists of two main modules, detection module and recognition module. | The recognition module utilizes character segmentation and end-to-end recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The proposed system is composed of detection module and recognition module as shown in Fig. 1. | The combined results of two methods are sent to recognition module.
studies.Method architecture evidence: CTPN (Connectionist Text Proposal Network) [12] is chosen as the neural networks in detection module, which is robust in text detection under variant disturbance. | The recognition module chooses CRNN (Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network) [8] as its end-to-end recognition method and uses the information provided by the detection module to do character segmentation. | In this module, ResNet is used as the recognition neural networks.
studies.Methods:
- Text detection, computer-vision branch: MSER with geometric filtering and clustering of character regions
- Text detection, neural branch: CTPN; both results are combined (CTPN boxes refined, characters missed by MSER recovered)
- Recognition, branch 1: character segmentation from the MSER boxes and ResNet character classification
- Recognition, branch 2: CRNN on the whole code region
- Check-digit verification selects the output; verified results are used for online training of CTPN and CRNN
studies.Methods evidence: In the detection module, MSER [1] is chosen as the algorithm-based computer vision, which is both efficient and effective for container-code detection. | Therefore, the combination sub-module is responsible for optimizing the bounding box of CTPN and finding the missing character in the detection of MSER. | After segmentation, characters will be recognized one by one using neural networks based on ResNet[13]. | In this recognition module, the detected container-code region is regarded as a whole and recognized by CRNN which will generate a text string as its recognition result. | The combination sub-module will verify the two recognition results according to the check digit in the container-code, and output the recognition result which passed the verification.

studies.Title: Automatic Container Code Recognition from Multiple Views
studies.Venue: ETRI Journal
studies.Contributions:
- Proposes a multi-view container code recognition system, integrating results from five camera angles.
- Introduces a character-level integration and a decision-level fusion technique for code reconstruction.
- Uses classical methods: connected component analysis, SVM-based character recognition, and Niblack binarisation.
- Achieves 96.2% overall accuracy, significantly improving on single-view accuracy (as low as 39.5%).
studies.Contributions evidence: In this paper, we increase the accuracy of container code recognition using multiple views. | A character-level integration method combines recognized codes from different single views to generate a new code. | A decision-level integration selects the most probable results from the codes from single views and the new integrated code. | The recognition from single views achieved an accuracy of around 70% for the test images collected on a working pier, whereas the proposed integration method showed an accuracy of 96%. | [Table 1: single view, right: 39.51; proposed algorithm using multiple views: 96.20] Table 1. Recognition accuracies from single and multiple views.
studies.Methods:
- Preprocessing: manually calculated perspective transformation of all images, fish-eye correction for the left and right planes
- Single-view pipeline: appearance-based character detection (Adaboost), Niblack binarisation, CCA, SVM recognition on eight-gradient features; Hough transform to exclude the door bars on rear planes
- Multi-view fusion: character-level multiple sequence alignment (MSA using SeqAn), decision-level integration using variance and check digit tests
- Final selection among 6 candidate codes (5 views + 1 integrated result)
studies.Methods evidence: For all images, the perspective transformation is applied to make the codes appear at the correct angle. | The Adaboost algorithm is used for training the detector, and the training set includes more than 40,000 character images and 260 background images (also known as negative images) exerted from the container code images. | First, the input code image is binarized using Niblack's method, which was proven to be more effective in character segmentation over conventional binarization methods [8]. | The algorithm converts an input character image into an eight-gradient feature vector, and SVM classifies the feature vector as alphabet characters and numbers. | The decision-level integration finally selects one among six codes including the new code from the character-level integration.

studies.Title: A New Framework for Container Code Recognition by Using Segmentation-Based and HMM-Based Approaches
studies.Venue: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
studies.Contributions:
- Framework that isolates character blocks instead of single characters and classifies them as single- or multi-character blocks
- Segmentation-based recognition for single-character blocks, segmentation-free HMM recognition for multi-character blocks
- Recognises container codes with closely arranged characters, where character segmentation fails
studies.Contributions evidence: In this framework, after locating the code-character region, character blocks instead of characters are isolated from the background. | Furthermore, character blocks are classified into two categories, i.e. single-character block and multi-character block. | In details, a segmentation-based character recognition is adopted for the single-character block, while for the multi-character block, we proposed using the hidden Markov model to recognize the characters and no segmentation operation is needed. | With the proposed framework, the closely arranged characters in container code can be detected and recognized successfully.
studies.Methods:
- Code-region localisation: horizontal high-pass filter, adaptive threshold, connected component analysis and scan-line analysis
- Character-block isolation: local-threshold binarisation (logical level technique), connected components, estimate of the number of characters per block, alignment-mode check
- Single-character blocks: Gabor-filter features and nearest-template matching
- Multi-character blocks: sliding-window features and HMMs (Gaussian mixtures, Baum-Welch training, Viterbi decoding)
- Check digit computed from ISO 6346 when its match is unreliable
studies.Methods evidence: In this framework, code-character regions are first located by applying a horizontal high-pass filter and scan line analysis. | Considering that the images obtained outdoors are subjected to uneven illumination, a local threshold binarization method is adopted. | The template-matching method, where the nearest classifier is adopted, is used to classify each character with the extracted feature vector. | For multi-character blocks, a HMM-based character recognition is employed to recognize the characters. | Nevertheless, the check digit can be calculated by the previous 10 characters according to ISO 6346.
studies.Method class: Digital image processing and Machine learning
studies.Method class evidence: In this framework, code-character regions are first located by applying a horizontal high-pass filter and scan line analysis. | Finally, a segmentation-based approach is implemented for recognition of the characters in single-character blocks, and a hidden Markov model (HMM) based method is proposed for the multi-character blocks. | Once the parameters of each HMM are initialized, these parameters will be further updated by the embedded Baum-Welch algorithm [15].

studies.Venue: 4th International Conference on Mechatronics, Materials, Chemistry and Computer Engineering (ICMMCCE 2015)
studies.Contributions:
- Proposes a novel preprocessing model for container image enhancement based on colour gradient, connected domain analysis, and adaptive weighting.

studies.Title: Vision-based identification extraction for freight containers
studies.Venue: International Conference on Wavelet Analysis and Pattern Recognition
studies.Contributions:
- Method to extract the identification from back-surface images of containers, where much other information is printed
- Character grouping by height and distance of bounding boxes and by y-axis correlation; selection of the group by length and position
- Recognition with Tesseract
studies.Contributions evidence: In this paper, a generic method of extracting freight container's identifications is proposed, particularly on the back surface of the container. | After image pre-processing, an effective character grouping approach is developed with the heights and distances of bounding boxes as well as the y-axis correlation to detect freight container's identifications. | Subsequently, the OCR algorithm Tesseract is applied to recognize the identifications, which reaches the accurate rate of 90.39%.
studies.Methods:
- Binarisation, connected component labelling, character grouping, y-axis correlation
- Tesseract for recognition.
studies.Methods evidence: Therefore, we first convert the input image into a grayscale image, and a multi-valued segmentation procedure is performed afterwards. | At the beginning, the connected-component labeling method proposed by Suzuki et al. is adopted [4], which groups the neighboring pixels in an image together. | After image pre-processing, an effective character grouping approach is developed with the heights and distances of bounding boxes as well as the y-axis correlation to detect freight container's identifications. | Finally, the OCR algorithm Tesseract is applied to recognize the characters of the group [5].
studies.Method class: Digital image processing and Machine learning
studies.Method class evidence: Therefore, we first convert the input image into a grayscale image, and a multi-valued segmentation procedure is performed afterwards. | At the beginning, the connected-component labeling method proposed by Suzuki et al. is adopted [4], which groups the neighboring pixels in an image together. | Finally, the OCR algorithm Tesseract is applied to recognize the characters of the group [5].

studies.Other text / markings near the code evid: It is clear that the freight container's identifications are impressed on its surface directly, and some other texts and advertisements may be marked on the freight containers. | This additional information often affects the accuracy of extracting freight container's identifications. | The reason for such a result is that the OCR algorithm recognizes the detected characters that pertain to the other information, not to freight container's identification, and only the first character is successfully recognized.
studies.Corrugated surface evidence: Some car bodies are not flat, such as trucks and freight containers, which increases the difficulty for character recognition.
studies.Check-digit frame evidence: It is found that the 11th character is also a code, most of which are bounded with a outer frame in the same color as the character for better recognition by humans, as shown in Figure 12. | The thin outer frames can be eliminated during the image pre-processing, but the thick outer frames will be merged into the character. | Training the OCR system using sample characters to increase the accurate rate of recognition: most of the failure cases are caused by an outer frame printed around the check code of freight container's identification.
studies.Variable code arrangement / format evide: Unlike car license plates, freight container's identifications have different colors and alignments. | Although many different kinds of text colors, background colors, and text compositions exist in freight containers, there are some common cues of their identifications.
studies.Variable character spacing evidence: The character intervals in the identifications are varied from each other, and other information such as advertisement and logos are also marked on the car body, which make it hard to recognize characters too.
studies.Character size variation evidence: The resolution of all the sample images is 600 × 500, each of whose contents is dissimilar to the others owing to different shot distances and angles.

studies.Font variation evidence: Compared car license plates with freight container's identifications, the former have unified formats and styles, but the latter have different styles, fonts and background colors, which is shown in Figure 2.
studies.Character segmentation errors evidence: Through the above observation, the causes of failures are mainly at the step of mutli-valued segmentation in image pre-processing, which makes it unable to perform character grouping. | The thin outer frames can be eliminated during the image pre-processing, but the thick outer frames will be merged into the character.

studies.Contributions: Object clustering method to localise each line of the ID code.
studies.Contributions evidence: In this paper firstly an object clustering method is proposed to localize each line of the container code region.
studies.Methods:
- Binarisation, morphological operations
- Object clustering
- OCR engine (not named) for recognition of the selected code region
studies.Methods evidence: The system architecture shown is achieved by the method of applying binary threshold, object clustering with analyzing objects area, width, height and length and finally setting a code location ratio condition between each line of code forming the container code region. | The threshold object is then connected to each other using Morphological closing operation with the structuring element constructed to form vertically connected image. | Thus in the algorithm, morphological operation bot-hat is being used to detect black color object. | Finally we feed the selected container code region to an OCR engine for recognition.

studies.Title: An automated vision system for container-code recognition
studies.Venue: Expert Systems With Applications
studies.Contributions:
- Proposes a full ACCR (Automatic Container Code Recognition) system composed of three major modules: text-line location, character isolation, and character recognition.
- Introduces a scanline-based method for locating text-line regions using a horizontal high-pass filter and scanline analysis.
- Uses a two-step segmentation strategy to tackle non-uniform illumination in outdoor container images.
- Implements SVM-based recognition using features extracted via Sobel edge filters and patch-wise edge densities.
- Evaluated on a large real-world dataset of 1214 container images.
studies.Contributions evidence: This technique consists of three function modules: location, isolation, and character recognition. | The first one is the scanline-based algorithm to extract text-line regions, which combines the vertical character edges and the spatial relationship between successive characters. | The second contribution is a two-step segmentation approach in the isolation module to tackle the severity of nonuniform illumination. | For each patch, the edge density is calculated as a feature. | Experiments are carried out with 1214 container images.
studies.Methods:
- Horizontal high-pass filter + adaptive thresholding + scanline grouping
- Edge-based binarisation + projection-based character segmentation
- Feature extraction via local Sobel gradients in 25 overlapping patches
- SVM classifier with RBF kernel for character recognition

studies.Title: Development of a container identification mark recognition system
studies.Venue: Electronics and Communications in Japan, Part 2
studies.Contributions:
- Gate camera system (trigger sensor, light-intensity sensor, illumination, shutter-speed control, colour filter) that copes with changing outdoor light and container colours
- Recognition scheme for differing code layouts based on the search for the letter U, multiplexed binary images and dynamic programming over character labels
- Field test of the complete device at the gate of a real pier with 601 images over five days
studies.Contributions evidence: The container number recognition system is constructed from an illumination intensity sensor and illumination system for handling the outdoor illumination changes, a shutter speed control device, and devices such as filters for handling various container colors. | In addition, the proposed system uses a character recognition scheme based on a dynamic design method for recognizing differing character string layouts in container marks or numbers. | Field tests were conducted using the proposed recognition device, installed at a real pier. | Six hundred one data items were obtained in 5 days.
studies.Methods:
- Camera system at the container gate: trigger sensor, light-intensity sensor, illumination for dark conditions, shutter-speed control, colour filter (G filter in the field test)
- Morphology filters (80 × 1 and 64 × 1 kernels) against long structures, binarisation at three thresholds (multiplexed binary images)
- Search for the letter U to infer polarity, character size and layout (horizontal or vertical); correlation-based string-region extraction when U is not found
- Character recognition: weighted directional index histogram features (48 dimensions) with a pseudo-Mahalanobis distance classifier
- Character-string recognition by dynamic programming over labels (the paper's dynamic design method); owner-code dictionary voting; check-digit frame removal
studies.Methods evidence: A morphology filter [23] having a kernel with a horizontal length of (80 × 1) is used to eliminate long components (such as metallic devices on the upper part of a container) in the horizontal direction and to perform binarization. | Three different binarized thresholds, 15, 30, and 45, are simultaneously generated at 256 gradations, an image processed with a threshold value of 30 is subsequently processed, and images processed with threshold values of 15 and 45 are used if the above image fails. | Character recognition uses weighted directional index histograms (4 directions, 48 dimensions) as features and the recognition scheme uses a pseudo-Mahalanobis distance method [19]. | Since the conventional assumption of “one label, one character” does not necessarily hold even in the recognition process after the extraction of a character string, a method of recognizing characters and cut characters simultaneously by dynamic design methods [15, 16, 18], involving address recognition and a subsequent English recognition system, is used. | By using a voting scheme based on a dictionary of owner codes prepared in advance to identify the character string in the dictionary to which a character string corresponds [21], owner codes not in the dictionary are not taken as solutions in recognizing the four English characters representing an owner.

studies.Contributions:

studies.Methods:
Preprocessing:
- Horizontal difference image with a tuned pixel distance, to preserve character edges
- Binarisation with an adaptive threshold (e.g. Otsu's method)
- Morphological erosion with adaptively sized structure elements to remove noise
Localisation:
- Horizontal projection with detection of local maxima
- Scan up and down from each maximum to delimit candidate text lines
- Filtering of candidate lines by pixel height, merging of overlapping lines

studies.Title: End-to-End Shipping Container Code Spotting Based on Visual Sensors for Intelligent Inspection
studies.Venue: IEEE Sensors Journal
studies.Contributions:
- End-to-end spotting framework for horizontal, vertical and multi-line (HVM) container codes in one model, aimed at autonomous inspection vehicles
- Inter-domain fusion network with self-spatial (SSEM) and self-channel (SCEM) enhancement modules on a lightweight ResNet backbone
- Transformer-based recognition heads with a character contrastive learning (CCL) loss
- 5125-image dataset from handheld, robot-mounted and gate cameras, announced as available on GitHub
- 91.2% F-measure and 93.2% recognition accuracy at 18.8 FPS
studies.Contributions evidence: We first propose an efficient end-to-end shipping CCS framework for HVM codes, which is effectively used in autonomous inspection vehicles. | An inter-domain fusion network that integrates the SSEM and SCEM is proposed to enhance the spatial and channel feature representations, thereby suppressing background noise and interference. | We introduce a transformer-based recognition branch with a CCL loss to strengthen character feature representation by capturing global contextual dependencies and enhancing the discriminability of character features. | Compared with existing methods, the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance with an F-measure of 91.2% and recognition accuracy of 93.2% in real-time. | [Section IV-A: complete sentence as printed (no full stop after the address)] The dataset is available at: www.github.com/giganticpower/CCRdata
studies.Main approach evidence: To address them, this article proposes an end-to-end CCS framework that combines detection and recognition into a unified model for HVM code recognition, allowing shared features to optimize both tasks.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The framework jointly optimizes detection and recognition within a single model by unifying the gradient flow.
studies.Method architecture evidence: We choose ResNet [53] as the backbone of the proposed model. | In the recognition head, we employ a six-layer transformer encoder to encode feature patches for each type of code, then transcribe the results [see Fig. 3(h)] through two fully connected layers.
studies.Methods:
- Backbone: ResNet18 pretrained on ImageNet
- SSEM (spatial attention with depthwise separable convolution) and SCEM (channel attention) fused into a shared feature map
- Detection head: segmentation of three code-type masks (horizontal, vertical, two-line) with dice loss, minimum bounding rectangles
- Masked RoI: type-specific feature patches (16×96 single-line, vertical codes rotated by 90°, 32×64 two-line)
- Recognition heads: one six-layer transformer encoder per code type, separate outputs for the 4 letters and the 7 digits, cross-entropy plus CCL loss
- Training augmentation: random rotation, scaling and horizontal flipping
studies.Methods evidence: The backbone is pretrained on ImageNet [54] for weight initialization. | The SSEM integrates a spatial attention mechanism with deep separable convolution (DSConv). | In the detection head, we perform 1 × 1 convolution on F f to reduce the channel dimension to 3 to predict the three types of code masks [see Fig. 3(f)]. | In the recognition head, we employ a six-layer transformer encoder to encode feature patches for each type of code, then transcribe the results [see Fig. 3(h)] through two fully connected layers. | In order to improve the generalization of the network, we use a variety of image enhancement methods (e.g., random rotation, random scaling, and random horizontal flipping).

studies.Venue: 2026 6th International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
studies.Contributions:
- Bi-headDet12: YOLOv12 without the low-resolution neck pathway and its detection head, for small BIC code regions
- DConvSTR: purely convolutional recogniser with a deformable convolution, trained with CTC loss and logit distillation from a GRCL teacher, without rectification or sequence modules
- Benchmark of 16 detector-recogniser pairs (RT-DETR, YOLOv10/11/12 with ABINet, ASTER, SRN, SVTR) on port CCTV data
- 1.75 M parameters and 2.97 GMACs at 100% exact-match accuracy
studies.Contributions evidence: To focus on the BIC code region, we propose Bi-headDet12, a lightweight detection model obtained by modifying conventional multi-scale feature utilization architectures. | We propose DConvSTR, a deformable convolution based recognition model trained via distillation to enable reliable string prediction without rectification modules or sequence based computation. | To clarify the comparative setup, we constructed a total of 16 two stage pipeline combinations by pairing the four selected detection models with the four selected text recognition models, and we analyzed the overall performance characteristics induced by detector recognizer coupling. | Compared with existing detection recognition combinations, VIC reduces parameters by up to 98% and computational cost (MACs) by up to 95% while maintaining 100% exact-match recognition accuracy.
studies.Main approach evidence: VIC is a simplified two-stage pipeline that detects the BIC code region in a container image and then recognizes the character sequence within it, using Bi-headDet12 for detection and a deformable CNN-based model for recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: We integrate the proposed detection and recognition models into VIC, a two-stage detect then recognize pipeline, and quantitatively validate both efficiency and performance through experiments on real-world port CCTV data.
studies.Method architecture evidence: Bi-headDet12 is a lightweight detection model that redesigns the YOLOv12 [16] object detector to better fit BIC code region detection. | In contrast, DConvSTR performs recognition using only convolutional operations, without an explicit rectification module or sequence based computation. | DConvSTR was trained using Connectionist Temporal Classification(CTC) loss [28], which is suitable for string prediction without explicit alignment, together with the Kullback Leibler (KL) divergence loss [18] to align teacher and student output distributions during distillation, and the Adadelta optimizer [29].
studies.Methods:
- Code region detection: Bi-headDet12 (YOLOv12-based, two detection heads; CIoU, DFL and BCE losses, SGD) on 640 x 640 images
- Code recognition: DConvSTR on 150 x 45 crops (deformable convolution, CTC loss, Adadelta)
- Knowledge distillation: KL divergence between the logits of a teacher with GRCL and the student
- Baselines: RT-DETR, YOLOv10, YOLOv11 and YOLOv12 combined with ABINet, ASTER, SRN and SVTR
studies.Methods evidence: Specifically, we remove both the neck pathway that processes and propagates the low resolution features and the corresponding detection head that consumes them. | During training, Bi-headDet12 used CIOU loss [25], Distribution Focal Loss [26], Binary Cross Entropy loss, and the Stochastic Gradient Descent(SGD) optimizer [27]. | DConvSTR was trained using Connectionist Temporal Classification(CTC) loss [28], which is suitable for string prediction without explicit alignment, together with the Kullback Leibler (KL) divergence loss [18] to align teacher and student output distributions during distillation, and the Adadelta optimizer [29]. | The teacher model incorporates a Gated Recurrent Convolutional Layer (GRCL) [19] in addition to deformable convolution to generate logits that reflect spatial contextual information. | For code string recognition, we cropped the labeled code regions and resized them to 45 × 150.
studies.Method class evidence: As shown in Fig. 1, the overall architecture of VIC consists of two main components: (1) Bi-headDet12, which detects the BIC code region from the input image and is based on the YOLOv12 [16] object detection architecture; and (2) Distilled Deformable Convolutional Network for Scene Text Recognition (DConvSTR), which takes the detected code region as input and predicts the BIC code string.

studies.Venue: Intelligent Data Engineering and Automated Learning – IDEAL 2024 (LNCS 15347)
studies.Contributions:
- Divide-and-conquer recognition: YOLOv7 reads the digits, EasyOCR the letters
- Multi-frame analysis: the three highest-confidence detection frames of a video are recognised and compared
- Re-annotation of a public Roboflow container dataset with all ISO 6346 fields

studies.Contributions evidence: This paper presents a divide-and-conquer approach for detecting container license plates, distinguishing between the identification of numbers and letters, and leveraging multiple video frames to improve detection performance. | In this approach, EasyOCR handles the recognition of letters, while YOLOv7 is used for digits. | For video streams, the system selects the three best frames - those with the highest confidence values - to proceed to the recognition phase. | Given the absence of existing datasets that comprehensively cover all the fields specified by the ISO standard for container identification, this dataset was enhanced with additional annotations to include all relevant ISO fields, aligning it with real-world requirements and enhancing the model's robustness and applicability. | Initial comparisons between YOLOv7 and YOLOv8 were conducted to determine the most suitable model.
studies.Main approach: Text detection, character detection and character recognition
studies.Main approach evidence: In the character recognition phase, the model processes cropped images of license plates from the detection phase to recognize characters. | To isolate and identify individual characters, we used the connected components technique. | In this approach, EasyOCR handles the recognition of letters, while YOLOv7 is used for digits.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: In this work, we propose and evaluate an ALPRI system designed to quickly and accurately identify license plates and recognize their characters, following the two-phase approach: the identification and recognition phases.
studies.Method architecture evidence: In this approach, EasyOCR handles the recognition of letters, while YOLOv7 is used for digits. [the paper does not describe the networks: YOLOv7 = CNN, EasyOCR = CNN, RNN, CTC by the chart's convention]
studies.Methods:
- Preprocessing: auto-orientation, resizing to 640 x 640, greyscale from the HSV value channel, Gaussian blur
- Code (licence plate) detection: YOLOv7 with transfer learning, chosen over YOLOv8; three highest-confidence frames per video
- Character preprocessing: 90° rotation of vertical codes, CLAHE, Gaussian blur, adaptive thresholding, morphological opening and closing
- Character segmentation: connected components
- Recognition: EasyOCR for letters, YOLOv7 for digits; outputs of the three frames compared for consistency

studies.Title: Automating Code Recognition for Cargo Containers
studies.Venue: Electronics
studies.Contributions:
- Two-stage pipeline of YOLOv7 (code detection) and TrOCR (recognition) that reads horizontal and vertical codes without orientation correction
- Data combining 3295 rail-terminal images from the Port of Sines with 2910 truck-gate images of a public GitHub dataset
- Comparison with Tesseract, EasyOCR and the deep text recognition benchmark, with and without YOLOv7
- Analysis by code orientation, error type and BRISQUE image-quality range
studies.Contributions evidence: Rather than relying on explicit orientation correction or rotation preprocessing, our approach integrates YOLOv7 for code detection and TrOCR for recognition, forming a robust pipeline. | The first dataset is provided by the Port of Sines Authority (PSA), while the second is open source from GitHub (Version: commit 4ff6f29) [21]. | Through experiments with Tesseract, EasyOCR, TrOCR, and the deep text recognition benchmark, this work identifies an effective combination that excels in these unique challenges of port environments. | To evaluate the effectiveness of the hybrid OCR system, this section analyses its performance under different text orientations and image quality conditions.
studies.Main approach evidence: An input image is processed by the detection stage, where YOLOv7 localizes the text regions of interest corresponding to the container codes. | Each cropped region is then fed into the recognition stage, where the TrOCR utilizes OCR to obtain machine-readable text.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: This architecture is divided into two main stages: the detection stage and the recognition stage. | The proposed pipeline operates sequentially, as shown in Figure 3.
studies.Method architecture evidence: The detection stages use the YOLOv7 model, a well-established architecture in real-time object detection. | The Transformer-Based OCR (TrOCR), developed by Li et al. [17], utilizes a Vision transformer (ViT) encoder and a text decoder, which allows it to learn visual patterns without relying on convolutional layers.
studies.Methods:
- YOLOv7 (36.5 M parameters) fine-tuned for code detection, frozen-backbone and unfrozen variants, 512×512 input
- TrOCR (trocr-base-stage1, ViT encoder and transformer decoder, 384 M parameters) fine-tuned on the cropped code regions
- ISO 6346 post-processing (check digit, size and type code), not used in the evaluation
- Baselines: Tesseract, EasyOCR, deep text recognition benchmark
studies.Methods evidence: To adapt the model, the YOLOv7 model was fine-tuned using the combined dataset. | First, with a frozen backbone to leverage the feature-extraction capabilities of the pre-trained model, and second, with an unfrozen backbone to allow the entire network to adapt to the specific characteristics of container code detection. | The recognition stage employs the TrOCR model, a transformer-based model, which has shown strong performance in various OCR tasks, particularly in handling complex scenarios. | This model verifies that the recognized container identification code is valid by calculating the check digit, confirming the structure is correct. | For comparison, the standalone OCR systems, Tesseract and EasyOCR, were also evaluated on the same test set, utilizing their default configurations to reflect their standard usage in practical settings.
studies.Method class: Digital image processing and Deep learning
studies.Method class evidence: To address these issues, this work proposes a hybrid Optical Character Recognition system that integrates YOLOv7 for text detection with the transformer-based TrOCR for recognition of the container codes, enabling accurate and efficient automated recognition. | Following the recognition stage, the post-processing step performs a validation ensuring compliance with the ISO 6346 standard. | This model verifies that the recognized container identification code is valid by calculating the check digit, confirming the structure is correct. | Although this step is essential for real-world deployment and integration into port management systems, it was not included in the model performance evaluation, as it does not directly affect model accuracy.

studies.Contributions:
- FLASS: first framework that spots container codes together with types, weights and hazard signs, in horizontal, vertical and multi-line forms
- YOLOv8-SL attribute detector (R2NFN backbone of Res2Net and FasterNet blocks): 98.44% AP50 with 17% fewer parameters and 14% fewer FLOPs than YOLOv8n
- SL-TD text detector for dense weight text and a rule-based text orientation correction (TOC) for vertical and two-line codes

studies.Contributions evidence: In this article, a fast and lightweight automatic shipping container attributes spotting (FLASS) is proposed for the first time to detect and recognize arbitrary-oriented container codes, types, weights, and hazard signs. | YOLOv8-SL achieves significant improvements in precision, reaching 98.44%, while reducing the model size by 17% and computational complexity by 14% compared to the original YOLOv8 model. | The permutation [L1][L2][G1][G2] achieved the highest word accuracy at 98.08% with 5.98 million parameters, indicating it provides the best performance among the tested configurations. | Extensive experimentation demonstrated that FLASS, comprising these three distinct models, achieves remarkable accuracy of 96.29%, offers high-speed inference at 32.71 FPS, and utilizes a lightweight model with just 10.3 million parameters. | The core concept of our method has been deployed and operational at gates, tallying stations, and gantry cranes at Ningbo Zhoushan Port for months, demonstrating practical application capabilities.

studies.Processing strategy evidence: The core foundation of the FLASS (see Fig. 2) is designed to automate the detection and recognition of shipping container attributes through the utilization of three primary models: YOLOv8-SL for object detection, SL-TD for TD, and SVTR-R for STR.
studies.Method architecture evidence: The proposed YOLOv8-SL (see Fig. 3) adopts the YOLOv8 nano architecture as its foundation due to its lightweight design and high efficiency, which are essential for real-time processing in resource-constrained environments. | SVTR [33] stands out for its innovative adoption of vision transformer (ViT) [39], combined with its compact design and exceptional processing speed. | [Fig. 5: the recogniser ends in a CTC head] Fig. 5. Overall structure of the proposed SVTR-R. The network is organized into four stages, where the height progressively decreases across three stages. Each stage involves a sequence of mixing blocks followed by a merging or combining operation. Finally, recognition is performed using a CTC head.
studies.Methods:

studies.Contributions:

- Arbitrary Angle Quadrilateral Fitting (AAQF) to fit tilted text regions before perspective correction

studies.Contributions evidence: In this study, we address these challenges by introducing an Enhanced OCR (EOCR) system, incorporating Line Segmentation Mask (LSM)-based detection and Scanline-based recognition. | Additionally, we propose the arbitrary angle quadrilateral fitting algorithm targeting sloping quad areas in images taken at a container terminal. | In contrast to many other LSTM blocks or RNN modules (which include multiple units within one layer), our attention layer contains only one LSTM cell, as shown in Fig. 11. | Finally, we added the image preprocessing step to these methods (see the fourth row of Table 4), which allows our model to perform to a rate of accuracy as high as 98.7%. | We used 10,000 images for the training set and 2000 as the test set.

studies.Method architecture evidence: To improve the detection accuracy of masking text areas in adjacent text rows, a line segmentation mask (LSM) module based on ResNet (He et al., 2016) backbone is designed to distinguish the text area from the non-text area pixel by pixel correctly. | The network architecture of Recognition Neural Network consists of three components: the convolutional layers, the attention layers, and a transcription layer, as shown in Fig. 9. | Inspired by previous studies (Lin et al., 2022; Shi et al., 2018; Wojna et al., 2017), we develop an LSTM-based attention mechanism as our recognizer. | We utilize the conditional probability framework outlined in the Connectionist Temporal Classification layer proposed by Graves et al. (2006).

studies.Contributions:
