studies.Contributions evidence: This paper focus on how to balance the accuracy and speed for the real-time video container numbers recognition during monitoring. | In order to meet the real-time requirements, the feature extraction part of DBNet is modified to the lightweight network MobileNetV3, the feature fusion part is modified to the FPEM and FFM module, and the loss function is modified to DiceLoss; The feature extraction part of SAR is modified to lightweight network MobileNetV3, the sequence feature extraction part is modified to GRU module, and more data augmentation modules are added to enhance the generalization ability of the model. | In this chapter, the text detection network EAST and PAN and recognition network CRNN and SRN are compared and evaluated on the container number recognition data set. | It has 4000 pieces in total, the ratio of training set and test set is 9:1. | In the case of reasoning using the shortest edge 1080, the recognition time is about 200ms, the accuracy is more than 95%, and the occupied video memory is about 2G.

studies.Contributions evidence: In order to promote the intelligent development of port, this paper proposes a container number recognition method based on SSD combined with SVM classifier, and designs a container truck detection program based on frame difference method and decreasing sequence of connected domain, which is used to capture the key frame image of container truck parking; for container number recognition, SSD_MobileNet is used to detect container number area, and the HOG feature of image is used to train the SVM classifier. | This paper proposes an image text correction method based on affine transformation. | Because the container number is composed of letters and numbers, in order to improve the recognition accuracy, this paper proposes a method of cooperation between number classifier and letter classifier. | The accuracy rate of box number area detection and container number recognition can reach 97% and 94.6% respectively.

- Preprocessing: aspect ratio decides vertical or horizontal code; connected regions filtered by area, width and height to remove noise
- Recognition: HOG features and SVMs with Gaussian kernel, separate letter and digit classifiers chosen by character position

studies.Venue: Journal of Physics: Conference Series (ICAITA 2020)
studies.Contributions:
- Improved EAST detector that predicts the container-number region directly, without candidate boxes
- Modified output layer (head/tail boundary pixels regress two vertices each) for long vertical code lines
- Instance-balanced dice loss (PixelLink style) and a boundary loss term weighted by the distance to the box edge
- Lightweight backbone with ShuffleNet channel shuffle and depthwise separable convolution
- 97.5% mAP at 14 FPS (96% at 19 FPS for the lightweight variant) on 6,000 test images
studies.Contributions evidence: In view of the above problems, the main contributions of this paper are drawing on the EAST text detection method to obtain an improved EAST algorithm that directly predicts the box number area. | This new algorithm not only eliminates multiple intermediate stages, but also improves the regression method and loss function of the box number area, optimizes the boundary, balances positive and negative samples to adapt to the detection area of the box number based on the original algorithm. | At the same time, it adopts the lightweight design idea, and uses ShuffleNet's channel shuffling and depth separable convolution for reference to optimize the original model, which reduces the complexity of time and space, compresses the model and reduces the detection time. | The final experimental results show that the accuracy of the algorithm reaches 97.5% while keeping the FPS index no less than 14. | In the final lightweight algorithm, while the accuracy is only slightly reduced (from 97.5% to 96%), the time complexity is greatly reduced, even the detection speed is greatly improved, from 14 frames / second to 19 frames / second, and perfect results are achieved in both accuracy and speed.
studies.Main approach evidence: In view of the above problems, the main contributions of this paper are drawing on the EAST text detection method to obtain an improved EAST algorithm that directly predicts the box number area. | The procedure of the whole box number detection algorithm is to roughly locate the whole box number area, then fine locate the rough detection area, and finally complete the combination of character lines to lay a solid foundation for the subsequent recognition.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: This new algorithm not only eliminates multiple intermediate stages, but also improves the regression method and loss function of the box number area, optimizes the boundary, balances positive and negative samples to adapt to the detection area of the box number based on the original algorithm.
studies.Method architecture evidence: In order to improve the accuracy of East detection, the residual network of RESNET is used to replace the VGg network in order to deepen the depth of the network. | Therefore, this paper uses the channel shuffle strategy of ShuffleNet[16] for reference, and then combines the depth separable convolution to build a lightweight East network.
studies.Methods:
- Rough positioning of the code area first (method not described), padding to fit the network
- EAST with ResNet instead of VGG-16, then lightweight channel-shuffle + depthwise separable convolution units
- 7-channel output: text score, head/tail flags, vertex offsets of the box ends
- Dice loss with instance balance and a training mask that drops boxes below a size threshold
- Boundary optimisation: distance-weighted cross-entropy once the dice loss falls below L_lim
- Baselines: original EAST, HOG+SVM, YOLO, SSD

studies.Contributions:
- Coarse-to-fine localisation of the container code region with mathematical morphology, region analysis and projection

- Verification of candidate code areas by the frequency of grey-level changes

studies.Contributions evidence: An automatic extraction method of container identity codes based on mathematical morphology operation, region analysis and projection transformation is proposed. | There are 6 possible arrangement types, according to which 6 combination of rectangles are designed to find the code area. | At last, the change frequency of the gray value of the image is used to identify the last code areas. | And the following results we obtained: the correct rate is 98.61%, the refused rate is 1.16%, and the error rate is 0.23%. | And the average time for every image is 17.2ms.
studies.Methods:
- Coarse location: morphological dilation minus erosion (circular structuring element), binarisation, closing with a 3 x 3 element
- Fine location: closed-region (boundary-tracing) search, horizontal and vertical projections to split and merge regions into rectangles
- Combination type test: rectangles matched to six arrangement patterns by position, width and height
- Location identification: black-to-white transition frequency within fixed ranges per rectangle
studies.Methods evidence: If we subtract the erosion image from the dilation one, we will get an image with the characters made prominent. | To eliminate the holes and strokes in Fig.4, the morphological closing is used. | Connected regions are found, and then projection transformation is used to split the region into a series of rectangles. | We can detect these 6 cases by the position, the width and the height of the rectangles. | At last, the frequency of the change from black to white of the binarized image in the rectangle area is used to identify if it is the code area.

studies.Title: Recognition of Shipping Container Identifiers Using ART2-Based Quantization and a Refined RBF Network
studies.Venue: International Conference on Adaptive and Natural Computing Algorithms (ICANNGA 2007), Lecture Notes in Computer Science 4432
studies.Contributions:
- ART2-based colour clustering and quantisation to separate identifier areas from background noise
- Direction-dependent binarisation that suppresses the shadows of the corrugation bends
- Refined ART2-based RBF network (fuzzy-adjusted vigilance, delta-bar-delta learning rate) for character recognition
- Identifier-area extraction 94% (vs 69.6% of an earlier method) and 3089 of 3102 characters recognised on 300 images
studies.Contributions evidence: This paper distinguishes identifier areas from background noises and removes noises by using an ART2-based quantization method and general morphological information on the identifiers such as color, size, ratio of height to width, and a distance from other identifiers. | For horizontally-arranged areas, to remove noises caused by bends, the iterative method is applied twice in the vertical and the horizontal directions separately and two outputs are combined by using AND image operation to one binarized area. | In the proposed ART2-based RBF network, the refined ART2 algorithm is applied to the middle layer of RBF network, which dynamically adjusts the vigilance parameter by using the fuzzy logic connection operator, and the learning ratio is dynamically adjusted by applying the delta-bar-delta method to the learning between the middle and the output layers of RBF network. | Experiments using 300 container images showed that 282 areas of identifiers and 3102 individual identifiers were extracted successfully. | The proposed RBF network recognized 3089 identifiers.
studies.Methods:
- ART2 clustering of RGB colours and quantisation to predefined colour bins
- 8-directional contour tracking for candidate identifier areas
- Noise removal by height-to-width ratio, distance between candidate areas and colour
- Iterative binarisation, applied in two directions and combined by AND for horizontally arranged areas
- Character extraction by 8-directional contour tracking
- Refined ART2-based RBF network for the recognition of owner-code letters, serial digits and check digits
studies.Methods evidence: In this paper, at first, color information of a container image is clustered by using the ART2 algorithm [3] and is quantized based on the predefined bin vectors, then the 8-directional contour tracking method [4] is applied to the quantized image. | So, the first type of noise-removal method removes noise areas by using the ratio of height to width. | In the second type of noise-removal method, after measuring the distance between candidate areas, areas being apart over the given interval from other ones may be removed as noises, and identifier areas are selected from remaining candidates by using color information. | For horizontally-arranged areas, to remove noises caused by bends, the iterative method is applied twice in the vertical and the horizontal directions separately and two outputs are combined by using AND image operation to one binarized area. | This paper proposed a refined ART2-based RBF network for the recognition of container identifiers.

studies.Contributions:

studies.Contributions evidence: In this paper we present a study of four segmentation algorithms with the aim of extracting characters from containers. | We compare their performance using images acquired under real conditions and using results of human operators as a model to check their capabilities. | After these first results, we thought it would be a good idea trying to merge the best two algorithms into one, in order to get benefits from both. | [Table 3: row 0 missed characters: LAT-Thr. 237, LWT 253, LAT-Wat. 253 images] Table 3: Performance of the improved algorithms, compared with the two algorithms with best results.
studies.Methods:
- Watershed segmentation (no parameters)
- LAT: local adaptive thresholding with the local mean, k from 0.9 to 1.6, union of the segmentations
- Global thresholding with k from 20 to 220, union of the segmentations
- Local variation (Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher) modified to merge regions by mean intensity, similarity 70% to 85%
- Each algorithm except local variation run once for white and once for black characters; geometric filter on aspect ratio, area, height and width
- Merged algorithms: LAT-Watershed, LAT-Thresholding, LAT-Watershed-Thresholding
studies.Methods evidence: As mentioned before, we have implemented and compared four different algorithms. | For LAT we used a value of k in the range of [0.9, 1.6] with a step value of 0.03, which makes a total of 23 segmentations per image. | We used the mean intensity of the region to decide whether two regions should merge or not instead of the variance as in the original algorithm. | With a geometrical filter we removed any object which did not meet the geometrical properties we expect of any character in the code (aspect ratio, minimum area size, height and width). | We repeated the tests taking both LAT and watershed algorithm as the basis of our merged algorithm.

studies.Title: Advanced vehicle monitoring in smart port utilizing deep denoising real-time object detectors integrated multi-resolution attention-augmented CRNN
studies.Venue: Ain Shams Engineering Journal
studies.Contributions:
- Y12-MRDnCRNN: deep denoising, YOLOv12 detection, multi-resolution enhancement and an attention-augmented CRNN reading truck and trailer licence plates and container IDs
- Gate-camera dataset from Vietnamese ports: 4,187 licence-plate images and 3,326 container-ID images
- Per-condition evaluation, ablation, statistical comparison with ViT, ResNet + Transformer, Tesseract and PaddleOCR, and LP benchmarks (AOLP, UFPR-ALPR)
- Smart-gate system at Hai Phong port (two lanes, edge devices), gate passage reduced to 15-25 s
studies.Contributions evidence: In this study, we develop a novel approach utilizing the integration of a DD technique, MR, and attention augmented CRNN (AA-CRNN) to detect and recognize LPs for container trucks and trailers and container IDs. | This dataset contains 4187 images of container trucks and trailer LPs and 3326 images of container identification (ID) numbers. | To validate the robustness of the proposed model, we conduct experiments using the AOLP (Table 7) and UFPR-ALPR datasets (Table 8). | The recognition algorithm has been integrated into the smart gate system deployed at Hai Phong Port. | As a result, the total time for each truck to pass through the gate area is reduced to just 15–25 s.
studies.Main approach evidence: YOLOv12 is employed to detect and localize vehicle LPs and container IDs in the images. | The processed images are then passed through an AA-CRNN, which enhances the model's focus on important image regions, extracts features for character sequence prediction, and decodes the sequence to produce the final output.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The input surveillance video is processed using a DD model to remove noise and artifacts. | YOLOv12 is employed to detect and localize vehicle LPs and container IDs in the images. | The MR approach is deployed to enhance the low-quality image to a high-quality one after extracting the LP region.
studies.Method architecture evidence: To address noise prevalent in port environments, we employ DnCNN as the preprocessing step. | For ROI (region of interest) detection, we leverage YOLOv12 [37], enhanced with an area attention mechanism and MR capabilities via feature pyramid networks (FPN). | This architecture includes CNN blocks for feature extraction, followed by an attention mechanism, bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU), and dense layers for sequence decoding. | The model is trained using the Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss, defined as:
studies.Methods:
- DnCNN deep denoising of the surveillance frames (fine-tuned on port-specific noisy-clean pairs)
- YOLOv12 with area attention and FPN multi-scale features detects three classes: vehicle_plate, trailer_plate, container_id
- Multi-resolution (MR) enhancement of the region: greyscale, thresholding, skew correction, dilation, bicubic super-resolution
- AA-CRNN: region resized to 256 x 64, ResNet-18 with CBAM and multi-head self-attention, spatio-temporal attention over previous frames, uncertainty-aware feature fusion, BiGRU (256 units), CTC loss
- 80/20 train/test split; evaluation per condition (ideal, low light, motion blur, perspective distortion, partial occlusion)
studies.Methods evidence: To address noise prevalent in port environments, we employ DnCNN as the preprocessing step. | For ROI (region of interest) detection, we leverage YOLOv12 [37], enhanced with an area attention mechanism and MR capabilities via feature pyramid networks (FPN). | If there is a skew in the document images, the skew correction technique is used to rectify the skew angles from the document images. | The output of the AA-CRNN is fed into a BiGRU (256 units, dropout 0.3) and a dense layer (37 units, softmax) to predict the character sequence. | The dataset is split into 80 % training and 20 % testing sets.
studies.Method class evidence: To address noise prevalent in port environments, we employ DnCNN as the preprocessing step. | For ROI (region of interest) detection, we leverage YOLOv12 [37], enhanced with an area attention mechanism and MR capabilities via feature pyramid networks (FPN). | As shown in Fig. 2, the CRNN is augmented with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance feature extraction for intricate sequences like container IDs. | The MR approach is deployed to enhance the low-quality image to a high-quality one after extracting the LP region.

studies.Title: An Inland Port Monitoring System using Aerial and Ground Imagery
studies.Venue: 1st German Robotics Conference
studies.Contributions:
- Inland-port monitoring system (Alberthafen, Dresden) combining UAV overview flights (orthophotos) with sensor-equipped reach stackers
- Three-stage transportation unit (TU) identification: YOLOv5-S TU detection, DBNet++ text detection within the TU regions, TrOCR recognition
- TRUDI dataset with 25,941 labelled instances in five classes (container, trailer, tank-container, logo, ID text)
- Preliminary per-stage results: TU mAP@50 71%, text detection F1 85%, CER 0.02

studies.Title: Maximizing Recognition Reliability: TrOCR Outperforms PaddleOCR in Challenging Container Automation Environments
studies.Venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science (IJRISS)
studies.Contributions:
- Two-stage pipeline: YOLOv10-S detects the container and the container-number and ISO-code regions, fine-tuned PaddleOCR or TrOCR reads the crops
- Comparison of a speed-optimised (PaddleOCR) and an accuracy-optimised (TrOCR) recogniser on images from a real port terminal gate
- Recognisers trained separately per text type (container number, ISO code) and, for TrOCR, per orientation (vertical, horizontal)
- TrOCR more accurate (98.73% / 71.17% exact match for ISO codes / container numbers), PaddleOCR faster (up to 18.35 FPS)
studies.Contributions evidence: This study developed an automated pipeline combining the YOLOv10 object detector for text region localization with fine-tuned PaddleOCR and TrOCR models for recognition. | Evaluation was conducted on a test set of 173 real-world images from an actual port terminal gate deployment after training on 8,899 augmented images. | The training was highly specialized to handle extreme real-world challenges (e.g., rotation, faded text), dividing the dataset by text type (ISO code vs. container number) and orientation (vertical vs. horizontal) to maximize recognition robustness. | TrOCR consistently demonstrated superior recognition accuracy, achieving 98.73% exact match for ISO codes and 71.17% for container numbers, exceeding PaddleOCR (97.42% and 70.14%). | However, PaddleOCR was significantly faster (up to 18.35 FPS for ISO codes) compared to TrOCR (7.93 FPS).
studies.Main approach: Object detection, text detection and text recognition
studies.Main approach evidence: Container Detection (YOLOv10-S): The YOLOv10 model was trained on the augmented dataset to serve as both a container detector and a text detector, localizing the container and precisely cropping the ROIs containing container numbers and ISO codes. | [Fig. 1: YOLOv10-S container detector, then YOLOv10-S text detector, then OCR (PaddleOCR / TrOCR) on the cropped regions] Figure 1: Overview process of container and ISO number recognition system with surveillance camera
studies.Processing strategy evidence: The methodology section outlines the experimental setup used to design, train, and evaluate a multi-stage automated container recognition system. | The container automation system was constructed as a two-stage pipeline:
studies.Method architecture evidence: Container Detection (YOLOv10-S): The YOLOv10 model was trained on the augmented dataset to serve as both a container detector and a text detector, localizing the container and precisely cropping the ROIs containing container numbers and ISO codes. | Training utilized the SimpleData format and leveraged Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) loss to handle distorted and irregularly spaced text. | Two distinct model configurations were tested: Config 1 prioritized accuracy, using the SVTR architecture augmented with a Spatial Transformer Network (STN) and 64 x 256 input pixel size, while Config 2 prioritized speed by omitting 48 x 256 pixels. | Conversely, TrOCR [10] (Transformer-based OCR) leverages complex Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture and self-attention mechanisms, excelling in accuracy by modeling contextual dependencies.
studies.Methods:
- Preprocessing: auto-orientation and resizing; augmentation by bounding-box cropping (3,407 to 8,899 images)
- Detection: YOLOv10-S (416 x 416 input) as container and text-region detector (container number, ISO code)
- Recognition A: PaddleOCR fine-tuned on the crops, SVTR with STN and CTC loss (Config 1, 64 x 256) or a speed configuration (Config 2, 48 x 256), separate models for container numbers and ISO codes
- Recognition B: TrOCR (ViT encoder, transformer decoder) fine-tuned on the same crops, split by text type and orientation

studies.Results:

- Test set (173 port-gate images): container detection 96.5% (167 of 173), text detection 97.6% (163)

- TrOCR: ISO code 98.73% (99.66%), container number 71.17% (94.13%)

OCR speed (Intel Xeon E5-2620v3):
- PaddleOCR 18.35 FPS (ISO code), 10.90 FPS (container number)
- TrOCR 7.93 FPS (ISO code), 3.55 FPS (container number)
Whole system:
- Overall recognition accuracy of YOLOv10 + TrOCR: 92% on the test set (not defined)

studies.Title: Vertically invariant network for vertical and horizontal scene text recognition
studies.Venue: Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence
studies.Contributions:
- Four-rotation convolution (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°) and a vertically equivariant ResNet-18 backbone (VE-ResNet) for vertical and horizontal text

studies.Contributions evidence: We introduced an 8-bit quantization technique for text detection and recognition models. | We introduced a quantization bias to the ground-truth labels to offset the quantization-induced error and improve the accuracy of the models. | We introduced a module specifically for text orientation detection to improve our recognition pipeline’s ability to process text that is oriented both vertically and horizontally. | We reduced the model size by a factor of 3.8x without significantly affecting the models’ performance. | Moreover, the optimized models were 1.6x faster, and the maximum RAM usage was 6.6x lower than the base models.

studies.Title: An Improved Character Recognition Framework for Containers Based on DETR Algorithm
studies.Venue: Sensors
studies.Contributions:
- DETR (transformer object detector) applied to the detection and recognition of container code characters
- ResNeSt-50 backbone with multi-channel split attention instead of ResNet-50
- Multi-scale location coding (MSLC) added to the sinusoidal position encoding
- Data augmentation simulating rain, snow, fog, smoke, occlusion and strong light, plus reconstruction of rare character classes
- 98.6% mAP@0.5 on a self-built container character test set
studies.Contributions evidence: The object detection algorithm DETR with transformers as the basic unit is introduced into the recognition of port container characters, which makes up for insufficient feature extraction and the poor anti-interference ability of model detection in the current widely used convolution operation. | In the backbone of the model, we introduce the split-attention structure on the basis of ResNet [11] and improve the feature extraction ability of the backbone through the connection method of multi-channel weight convolution. | With the introduction of multi-scale location coding (MSLC), the transformer structure no longer only focuses on the semantic information of input content, but gives consideration to both semantic and location information. | The filtering-based data enhancement method used in this paper can effectively solve the problem of insufficient data sample size under severe outdoor weather. | The test result in the self-built container character data set can reach 98.6%, which meets the requirements of the smart port for the detection accuracy of container numbers.
studies.Main approach evidence: An improved DETR (detection with transformers) object detection framework is proposed to realize accurate detection and recognition of characters on shipping containers. | In order to avoid confusion of character detection by non-target numbers in the rest of the container, this part of the image has undergone region detection and cropping before detection.
studies.Processing strategy evidence: [abstract: one network performs the one task of detecting and classifying the characters of the cropped code region; no code string is assembled or evaluated] An improved DETR (detection with transformers) object detection framework is proposed to realize accurate detection and recognition of characters on shipping containers.
studies.Method architecture evidence: To this end, we use ResNeSt as our backbone [13–15]. | The transformer framework used in this article consists of 6 encoders and 6 decoders.
studies.Methods:
- Code region detected and cropped beforehand (method not described)
- DETR-ResNeSt-MSLC: ResNeSt-50 backbone, fusion of four feature-map scales, multi-scale location coding plus sine encoding
- Transformer with 6 encoders and 6 decoders, 100 object queries, FFN heads for character class and bounding box
- Hungarian matching loss: cross-entropy classification, GIoU and L1 box losses
- Augmentation: simulated rain and snow (noise and filters), fog (atmospheric scattering model), smoke, random block occlusion, strong light (gamma transform and white balance)
- Small-sample reconstruction: rare characters (Z, W, V, P, N) pasted onto other samples (500 images)
- Training: 100 epochs on an NVIDIA Tesla V100

studies.Title: Accurate, Swift and Noiseless Image Binarization
studies.Venue: Statistics, Optimization and Information Computing
studies.Contributions:
- Histogram-based binarisation of the container-code region that decides automatically whether the characters are darker or lighter than the background
- Foreground boundary adjustment that keeps faint characters (e.g. a grey check digit) under mud, dust, shadows or fluid leakage
- Optional OCR mode with less noise that mostly removes the box around the check digit
- Evaluation on 400 back-side container images with a free online OCR against 21 ImageJ thresholding methods: 85.83% of code characters recognised versus at most 56.00%
studies.Contributions evidence: Our approach consists of transferring a colored image into grayscale, then to construct the histogram which will be divided into group of colors and after that, the foreground -that can be darker or lighter than the background- will be automatically identified and finally, the foreground boundaries will be assiduously enhanced before creating the binarized image. | Fig. 12 illustrates the case where the useful check digit number (i.e., rightmost number of the first line) has a gray color while the foreground is white which clarifies why some colors should be borrowed from the group adjacent to the foreground. | Even though our proposed method implicitly filters the binary image, it has the option to run for OCR applications and thus, the result image will contain much less noise and the useless box around the container check digit will be alleviated, or most of the times, removed. | To be objective in presenting our approach, we will introduce hereafter a table that contains a comparison between our proposed method and the other 21 methods; Figure 24 contains some statistics related to the result of using 400 randomly selected container images and it is worthy to note that the OCR that we used is freely accessible via the website http://www.onlineocr.net/. | [Fig. 24: row 'Our method': 3433 recognised container digits (85.83%); best other method, Sauvola: 2240 (56.00%)] Figure 24. An Objective Comparison.
studies.Methods:
- Input: upper-right part of the back-side image holding the code (how it is cut out is not described), greyscale conversion
- Histogram creation (256 bins), smoothing and division into groups of colours (one per hill)
- Foreground identification: background = group with the highest peak; groups left and right of it scored, the farthest group of the winning side is the foreground; disconnected extreme groups (sky, sun) and histogram values below 15 ignored
- Foreground boundary pinpointing: colours borrowed from adjacent groups (foreground at least 5% of the histogram length and of the pixels, at most 1/6 of the background length)
- Binary image creation; optional OCR mode with less noise and the check-digit box suppressed
- Evaluation: free online OCR (onlineocr.net) on the binarised images; 21 local and global thresholding methods of ImageJ as baselines

studies.Title: Smart Ship Container With M2M Technology
studies.Venue: The Journal of Korean Institute of Communications and Information Sciences
studies.Contributions:
- Container code identification at the terminal gate with OpenCV image processing and the Tesseract OCR engine, implemented in Visual Studio 2010
- Code region location for horizontal and vertical code formats, with skew correction
- Gate application with operator confirmation of the read code and automatic email alerts on container arrival and discharge
- Proposed ship-side alert system (GPS, Arduino, cloud upload outside cellular coverage), not tested
- Region location 96% (good images) and 91% (degraded images); average character recognition 89%
studies.Contributions evidence: Firstly, the paper introduces the container code identification and recognition algorithm implemented in visual studio 2010 with Opencv (computer vision library) and Tesseract (OCR engine) for real time operation. | Secondly the emailing function correctly sends email alerts to the container customers on the status of the container while the containers are in and out of the terminal yard. | region location algorithm showed accuracy of 96 | % for average good quality images and 91% for images with missing characters, damaged containers, blurry images, extra marks on the container, and with uneven position of the acquisition system. | The average recognizing rate was 89%.
studies.Methods:
- Segmentation: top-hat and bot-hat transforms extract white or black characters, chosen by the character colour
- Code region location: binarisation, connected component labelling, filtering by character width and height, morphological closing to join the characters, filtering by code length and height; horizontal or vertical format decided by closing with different structuring elements; bounding box
- Skew correction: rotated minimum bounding rectangle, affine transformation
- Preprocessing: top-hat/bot-hat, median filter, morphological closing

studies.Title: A classification architecture based on connected components for text detection in unconstrained environments
studies.Venue: 2009 Advanced Video and Signal Based Surveillance
studies.Contributions:
- Connected-component text detector for container codes on freight trains, also applied to car plates and ICDAR images
- 20 CC features (geometry, contour, stroke width, moments) classified as text or non-text with Regularized Least Squares
- Focus-of-attention architecture: cascades of single-feature and at-most-2-feature classifiers selected by kernel class separability, and a 2-layer cascade followed by one Gaussian RLS classifier
- Equal error rate below 2% on container-code CCs; the combined solution is 4 times faster than the single classifier
studies.Contributions evidence: The paper presents a method for efficient text detection in unconstrained environments, based on image features derived from connected components and on a classification architecture implementing a focus of attention approach. | The main application motivating the work is container code detection with the final goal of checking freight trains composition. | To this purpose we use a set of 20 features, most of them available from the literature. | Thus the method is rather general and it has been applied, not only to a dataset of container codes images (obtaining an equal error rate – e.e.r.– below 2%) but also to car plates images (e.e.r = 1.2%). | This combination allows us to reduce the amount of computation (only 20-30% of CC are evaluated with the unique classifier, making text detection four times faster).
studies.Methods:
- Segmentation: Niblack local thresholding (window 1/5 of the image size) into connected components
- CC description: 20 features (aspect ratio, occupy ratio, edge contrast, homogeneity, edge symmetry, run length, direction variations, contour roughness, holes, perimeter, correlation, stroke width, Zernike moments, generalised Fourier descriptor, normalised central and Hu moments)
- Classification: Regularized Least Squares with a Gaussian kernel, text versus non-text per CC
- Cascades: feature selection by Kernel Class Separability, minimum hit rate 99.5% per layer set by leave-one-out cross-validation
- Combined solution: 2 cascade layers (aspect ratio, edge strength), then one classifier on the remaining features
- Container training set mixed with car plate CCs (500+500 training, 970+40000 test CCs from container images)
studies.Methods evidence: Following a well established pipeline [16], the proposed method has been organized in three main stages: (1) image segmentation, (2) connected components description, (3) classification. | The classification architecture that we consider is based on Regularized Least Squares (RLS) — other regularized algorithms could be easily adopted, with some computational gain on the training phase [6]. | In this paper we apply a recently proposed feature selection technique: Kernel Class Separability [12]. | We implement a 2 layers cascade with the features aspect ratio and edge strength (the first two layers in the at-most-2-features cascade). | To deal with the text localization problem on the containers dataset we built a training set combining container and car plates data, while the test set is made of CC from containers images.

studies.Title: Recognition of identifiers from shipping container images using fuzzy binarization and enhanced fuzzy RBF network
studies.Venue: Soft Computing
studies.Contributions:
- Identifier-area extraction from a Canny edge map by vertical, then horizontal histograms
- Fuzzy binarisation of the identifier area against shadows, low contrast and uneven intensity
- Character extraction by 4-directional contour tracking and grouping into owner code, serial number and check digit, for horizontally and vertically arranged codes
- Enhanced fuzzy RBF network whose middle layer is an enhanced fuzzy ART network with adaptive vigilance parameter and learning rate
- 150 images: all identifier areas found, 1592 of 1650 characters extracted (1385 with the author's earlier method), 1587 of 1592 recognised
studies.Contributions evidence: The proposed algorithm, first, extracts the area containing only the identifiers from a container image by using CANNY masking and bi-directional histogram method. | The extracted identifier area is binarized by the fuzzy binarization method newly proposed in this paper. | Then a contour tracking method is applied to the binarized area in order to extract the container identifiers which are the target for recognition. | This paper also proposes an enhanced fuzzy RBF network that adapts the enhanced fuzzy ART network for the middle layer. | All 150 identifier areas were successfully extracted from container images and 1,592 identifiers were successfully extracted out of a total of 1,650 identifiers.
studies.Methods:
- Code localisation: Canny edge map, vertical then horizontal edge histograms to crop the identifier area
- Binarisation: fuzzy binarisation (membership interval from mean, minimum and maximum intensity of the area, alpha-cut 0.9)
- Character segmentation: 4-directional contour tracking with a 2x2 mask, noise removal by height-to-width ratio
- Code assembly: arrangement into one row by Euclidean distance, sequential grouping into owner code, serial number and check digit (ISO 6346); separate procedures for vertical and horizontal areas
- Character recognition: enhanced fuzzy RBF network, middle layer an enhanced fuzzy ART network (vigilance adjusted with Yager's intersection operator, adaptive learning rate), sigmoid output layer trained with the delta rule
studies.Methods evidence: Hence, we calculated the vertical coordinate of an identifier area by applying the vertical histogram to the edge map, and applied the horizontal histogram to the block corresponding to the vertical coordinate, calculating the horizontal coordinate. | In this paper, the four-directional contour tracking method using 2×2 mask was used considering the whole preprocessing time of a container image. | In this paper, the extracted identifiers are arranged in a single row by using Euclidean distances between identifiers and then classified into three code groups. | For the recognition of extracted identifiers, we proposed an enhanced fuzzy RBF network which constructs the middle layer using the enhanced fuzzy ART network. | The enhanced fuzzy ART network dynamically adjusts the vigilance parameter according to the homogeneity between the patterns using Yager’s intersection operator [11] which is a fuzzy connection operator.
